# City council approves funding for downtown transit hub

The city council voted 6 to 3 on Tuesday to approve $14 million in bond funding for a new transit
hub at Fifth and Main, ending a debate that has run since early last year. Construction is expected
to begin in March and finish by the end of 2027, according to the transit authority.

Council member Denise Okafor, who sponsored the funding measure, said the hub would consolidate
four existing bus routes and add a covered platform for the planned streetcar extension. "Riders
have been standing in the rain at three separate stops for years," Okafor said during the meeting.
"This puts them under one roof."

Opponents raised concerns about cost overruns on the authority's last major project, a maintenance
facility that finished 18 months behind schedule and $2.1 million over its original budget. Council
member Tom Vasquez voted against the measure, saying the authority had not shown it could deliver
projects on time.

Transit authority director Priya Raman disputed that comparison. She told council members the
maintenance facility delay stemmed from a permitting dispute with the county that has since been
resolved, and that the transit hub's design was already 90 percent complete before Tuesday's vote.

Construction will require closing the northbound lane of Fifth Street for roughly four months
starting in the spring. The authority said it will post detour signage and update its website
weekly once work begins. A public meeting on the construction timeline is scheduled for February 12
at the downtown library branch.
